campaign_id: qwen35-4b-w4a16 g1: the generated fragile suite as a baseline (2026-09-09)
question: Two things at once. Does the fragile suite built from f1's per-prompt rates deliver the event concentration it was designed for, and does the 9B lane's copy-group diagnostic replicate on a second model?
config: one B70, TP1, depth 3 and MTP0, draft INT4 head, pad off, capture 1-64, c64, 20 passes, the 16-prompt fragile suite run with --verbatim-prompts so each prompt occupies four slots with byte-identical text

finding_1_the_suite_works.statement: Against the full 2026-08-25 suite at the same rung, the fragile suite concentrates events about fourfold on both lanes: 53.98% against 13.28% at depth 3, and 2.73% against 0.70% at MTP0. That is what build-fragile-suite.py was for, and it is what makes the remaining intervention arms affordable.
finding_1_the_suite_works.caveat: These rates are not comparable to any full-suite number as absolute measurements. The suite is a deliberately biased instrument selected on measured rate; it compares arms, it does not characterise a configuration.

finding_2_the_copy_group_rate_replicates.statement: The 9B lane's MTP0 fragile campaigns give 23 of 240 copy-groups disagreeing, 9.58%. The 4B gives 32 of 320, 10.0%. Two different models, different fragile suites built independently from each model's own rates, and the same disagreement rate to within a few tenths of a percent.
finding_2_the_copy_group_rate_replicates.reading: Suggestive rather than settled - two points, and the suites differ in size - but if the rate is a property of the serving regime rather than of the model, that is worth knowing before anyone reads a change in it as a model effect.

finding_3_speculation_dominates_here_too.statement: Copy-group disagreement is 10.0% without speculation and 67.5% at depth 3 on the same suite and rung, and the oracle-free minority rate is 2.60% against 27.31%. The speculative lane is where this phenomenon lives.
finding_3_speculation_dominates_here_too.context: The 9B depth-3 lane reads 30.8% and 41.7% in its two fragile arms, so the 4B is worse at depth 3 while matching at MTP0.

finding_4_three_outputs_are_two_sites.statement: The depth-3 histogram includes 16 groups with three distinct outputs, which the MTP0 lane never produces. All 16 diverge at two distinct indices rather than one: they are cache-c016 (sites at 26 and 50) and capacity-c022 (17 and 93), the two prompts already independently known to carry a second site. A site remains binary everywhere; a prompt with n sites can show up to 2^n outputs, and only the higher-rate lane fires both often enough to see three.
finding_4_three_outputs_are_two_sites.why_it_matters: It closes what looked like a counterexample to the binary-fork model without weakening it.

context_from_the_9b_lane: The copy-group diagnostic is not this campaign's. experiments/qwen35-9b-b70/notes/2026-09-08-identical-prompts-in-one-batch-diverge-from-each-other.md introduced it, and the lane's settled reading is in 2026-09-08-a-lockstep-batch-is-deterministic-the-ladder-is-not.md: a constant-composition batch is deterministic and the divergence needs the composition to vary. Copies in a group are spread about three decode steps, so they do not share a composition, which is why they can disagree at all.
